rule.referenceSummarizer: opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor through upstream's e2_score.compress_one (CB_SUMMARIZER_API=chat, the local pass-through); upstream's default output cap
rule.maskTail: no model call: the session's transcript view, newest lines first, tool lines with their output cleared, cut to the candidate arm's S character count for the same session
rule.variant: every decision reads S (the memory block plus the kept messages, what the model sees after compaction); the block alone and the STM chunks are reported beside it, never decided on
rule.estimate: candidate minus comparator, points of retained details (recall x 100), paired per session
rule.interval: 95% bootstrap over sessions (each session one cluster), 10,000 resamples, seed 7

A.ship: STM + WM ships as the session default if WM vs the Claude Code prompt has interval lower bound >= -5 and WM vs memory-off has interval lower bound > 0
A.deterministic: if WM does not beat STM-only (interval lower bound <= 0), the deterministic WM policy is the default: the same retention, no WM model call
A.loses: if WM's interval upper bound is < 0 against the Claude Code prompt or anchor_index, the finding goes to the owner before any plan builds on WM; it holds the decision for the owner and does not change it
A.m5: M5 (WM vs STM-only, criteria nonInferior) reads the paired estimate over all sessions; the sessions where this screen's WM run engaged are reported beside it

B.ship: STM is supported as the session memory if session vs the Claude Code prompt has interval lower bound >= -5 and session vs memory-off has interval lower bound > 0
B.loses: if session's interval upper bound is < 0 against the Claude Code prompt or anchor_index, the finding goes to the owner; it holds the decision for the owner and does not change it
B.m5: M5 stays missing; the screen makes no claim about WM

rules.maskTail: if the candidate does not beat mask-tail (interval lower bound <= 0), the finding goes to the owner with the verdict; it decides nothing by itself
rules.notShown: a candidate that neither ships nor loses clearly ships nothing; the finding goes to the owner

cannotShow: one model family (Muse worker and summarizer)
histories are capped at 250,000 characters by upstream, so long-horizon WM behaviour is out of reach

findings: WM loses clearly against the Claude Code prompt or anchor_index: to the owner
WM is not shown to ship (non-inferior to Claude Code and above memory-off): to the owner
